workflow_hypothesis: Nonportable build-script commands and incorrect generated compiler flags
pattern: A build/configuration generator emits embedded text-processing commands using syntax that is not portable across supported tool dialects.
description: Build or configuration generation relies on shell-invoked text-editing commands whose syntax and multiline behavior vary between implementations.
precondition: The build system generates scripts or edit commands dynamically and may run with different implementations of the assumed text-processing utility.
critical_operation: The generated workflow invokes those commands to construct or modify configuration artifacts and build metadata.
interference: The target utility parses multiline edits or edit-script fragments differently from the implementation assumed by the generator.
invalid_assumption: The generator assumes that detecting or invoking a nominally compatible utility guarantees identical command syntax and semantics.
failure: Configuration aborts when edit instructions are rejected or interpreted as shell commands, leaving generated artifacts invalid and preventing the build from proceeding.
search_strategy: Inspect generated shell scripts for embedded multiline text-processing commands and verify their syntax against every supported utility implementation.
Check whether generated edit scripts rely on implementation-specific insert, append, or external-file semantics.
Run configuration generation with alternate utility implementations and inspect failures for edit instructions leaking into shell parsing.
Verify that generated configuration artifacts are syntactically valid immediately after each text-processing transformation.

evidence.supports: Documents a generated configuration edit using multiline insertion syntax that works with one utility dialect but is rejected by another, causing configuration failure.
Documents a generated configuration script containing an edit command fragment that the shell attempts to execute, producing a command-not-found and syntax error during configuration.

scope_note: The shared pattern is nonportable generated text-processing syntax causing configuration-script failure. One report also documents missing and incorrectly ordered compiler flags for shared-library objects, but that separate flag-propagation issue is not supported by the other report and is intentionally excluded.
